problems.problem: Literature FACTs overstate what the code matched. 'Of these 50 ... 4 an Asian population' counts R0179 only for 'Chinese Herbal Medicines' and R0055, a GLP-1 agonist review, for 'Indonesian health-care setting'. The headline 'Latest search end stated: May 2026' comes from an HFpEF phenotype review's publication window (R0002). Row 3's search end '2026' is a publication window. The DRAFT 'Partly covered: ... Asian people' rests on these matches.
problems.cause: Step 3 says to choose reviews 'by code ... using the focus's own terms and the topic's population terms' and to report 'the latest search end date among them'. It sets no precision rule for population matches and does not separate publication windows from search ends. Without the kit, the agent wrote a plain word matcher.
problems.fix: Add to Step 3: 'Count a population only when its words describe participants (for example "in Asian patients"), never journal names, settings or products. Require the intervention and a focus term in the title or the same sentence. Report the latest search end only among reviews that cover the focus, naming the review, and call a publication window a window. Describe each count by what the code matched, for example "4 abstracts contain Asian-population words".'

problems.problem: Kinds of purpose were lettered a-i inside numbered question 2. The persona, who picks numbers, answered '2 3'. The assistant mapped that to b and c (msg 14) and carried the guess into the certified Team's Purpose without an explicit confirmation of the mapping; the reason given was 'focus is right'. The persona said: 'I would have liked to see the list again instead of a guess.'
problems.cause: The prompt contradicts itself. The reply shape says 'Label options inside a numbered question a, b, c (never with digits)'. Step 2b says 'show the Team's Purpose states as numbered options' and asks for 'the numbers of the purpose types that apply'.
problems.fix: In 2b, write: 'Show the kinds of purpose as their own list numbered 1-9 (9 = other), outside the numbered questions, and ask "Which numbers apply?". If a reply uses digits for lettered options or letters for numbered ones, name the kinds you read under Done and ask for "yes" or the right names before building the certification line.'

problems.problem: Your turn asks 'Do these reviews change how you see your focus?' but the reply shows only a 3-bullet summary and sends the persona to the side file ('The full list of reviews is open beside the chat'). The persona: 'I would not open the file, so I cannot really judge.'
problems.cause: Two rules conflict: 'Never repeat a table ... already shown in this session' and 'whatever a question asks the team to judge is in the same reply'.
problems.fix: Add an exception to the no-repeat rule: 'except when Your turn asks the team to judge it: then show the rows it needs (at most 5: title, year, Says) in that reply, and never point to a side file instead.'

problems.problem: The answer to 'what was the search strategy?' pointed to the side file ('the full search cards are beside the chat'), which persona moment 9 forbids. The compact form also gave no plain one-line strategy per search that a terse user could read.
problems.cause: 'If your interface can show a file beside the chat, you may also open the one file under discussion there, and name it', together with 'give its compact form ... and offer show <item>'.
problems.fix: Write: 'When answering a question about something already shown, give the compact form in the chat (for each search, one line: source, topic or focus, the concepts joined by AND, the count) and offer "show <item>"; do not mention a side file in that reply.'

problems.problem: A wall of text: 4 code blocks, 3 card tables, a 10-row table, a coverage DRAFT and the 79-word CERTIFY line, with 351 prose words. The persona 'could not tell which part was "the search strategy" in plain words' and asked about it next, so goal 2 (see the strategy without asking) was only nominally met.
problems.cause: The Searches and Step 3 rules require full cards, a results table and a coverage DRAFT in the same reply, but nothing requires a plain-language summary of the strategy first.
problems.fix: After the FACT lines, add: 'Then one plain line per search: "<source>, <topic or focus>: <concept> AND <concept> ... -> <n> records [k]"; the full cards follow under the heading "Search details".'

problems.problem: The intake asked 6 things: name, a 'yes' to the topic, 3 questions and consent. The persona answered neither consent nor the topic, so the topic was asked again (msg 10). It then stayed 'to confirm' until it was folded into the Team's Purpose line, which was certified with a reason about the focus only.
problems.cause: Step 2a already requires name, 3 questions and consent; Step 1's 'a summary they confirm' adds a separate topic confirmation.
problems.fix: In Step 1 and 2a, write: 'Do not ask separately to confirm the topic; the 2b reflection restates it and its "yes" confirms it. State consent as a default ("I keep summaries unless you say exact words") rather than as a question.'

problems.problem: Item 1 combined the reflection 'yes' with a population either-or ('If the reflection is right, choose a or b ... If it is wrong, choose c'), and item 3 combined two asks. 'yes. 2 3. yes' left the population unresolved. The persona: 'Question 1 asks about a population limit, which I never raised, and I don't see why it matters.'
problems.cause: Step 2b asks for one reply covering the reflection, the purpose numbers and the motivation states, plus a population either-or and a learning either-or, each as its own item. That is more than 3 items, which forces bundling.
problems.fix: In 2b, write: 'Never put two asks in one numbered item. Ask the population either-or in the reply after the reflection is confirmed, with one clause on why it matters (it decides whether Step 3 searches that population).'

problems.problem: The 79-word Team's Purpose CERTIFY line was shown in full in four replies in a row (msgs 18, 20, 22, 24) while the persona deflected. It drove the turn-length median to 237 and read like a form to retype ('I don't want to retype or write anything more').
problems.cause: 'Whenever Your turn asks for a certification, show the line just above Your turn in that reply, even if you showed it before.' In addition, the topic wording rides in the Team's Purpose line ('keep the item marked (to confirm) until it enters a certification line').
problems.fix: Write: 'Show the full line the first time and whenever its wording changes; otherwise write "The Team's Purpose line above is unchanged; reply certify and say why."' Keep the topic out of the purpose line by confirming it in the 2b reflection.

problems.problem: The first planning reply carried set-up talk ('the small test file from my first turn is no longer here ... I will give you a package'), against persona moment 1 ('No set-up chatter'). The persona called it 'a bit of noise'.
problems.cause: R11: 'If your files may not persist, say so at the start'.
problems.fix: Change R11 to: 'If your files may not persist, say so in one clause in the first To save block or at the first pause, not in the Step 1 reply.'

problems.problem: OpenAlex requests L000077-L000079 failed with HTTP 429 (a rate limit for boolean queries with more than 5 operators). They were re-run as L000085-L000087 without refers_to links or a note. The Sources lines say 'run 2026-10-24' while the log's time_utc is 2026-10-25T03:35Z, and nothing says that is a local date. The OpenAlex code block also omits the 'title_and_abstract.search:' prefix and the date filter actually sent.
problems.cause: Section 3.5 covers corrections but not failed requests or retries. Section 3.4 does not mention OpenAlex's boolean rate limit. The Searches rule asks for 'the exact string as run' but sets no date convention.
problems.fix: Add to 3.5: 'Log a failed request with its HTTP status; its retry refers_to it.' Add to 3.4: 'Without a key, space OpenAlex boolean queries at least 1 second apart.' Add to Searches: 'Show OpenAlex's full filter as sent, and give run dates in UTC or label them "local date".'

judge.strengths: Certification handling is strong. A bare 'Certify' got exactly the reason question; 'just start' was not treated as approval; each certification was logged, committed under the neutral identity and shown back with the reason as given. The research focus was found through the one-question probe, reflected back with 'Added by me: nothing', reconciled when it narrowed, and carried into the status line, the purpose line and the Step 3 focus search. The early move was announced and flagged in the status line, and Step 3 questions waited under Next. Every counted search was shown in full, with code-block strings, per-block counts, a Create Date bound checked in PubMed's query translation, Sources and what was not searched. Every number reproduces from saved raw files (all 26 recounts match; byte-for-byte notebook re-run). Consent and privacy were respected: summaries only, no email or key in files, and an OpenAlex prompt-injection notice treated as data. The pause produced a summary, the plan map and the package only at that point.
